knownLimitations.reason: MmsServerConnection_sendInformationReportListOfVariables encodes a wrong length (2 trailing bytes); the adapter sends only VMD named-list reports
LIB61850-557 rejects initialPosition past EOF, but an in-range position is still not seeked; the test asserts the unseeked content
only scopeOfDelete specific is implemented; bulk deletes are answered with an Access-class ServiceError
the server fetches the source file from the client with FileOpen/FileRead (role reversal), which go-mms does not serve; the request fails with a File-class ServiceError
the client's FileOpen response handler leaves lastModified uninitialised when the optional field is absent; the test asserts size and content only
iec61850bean server does not expose SBOw[CO] as a writable MMS attribute

mms.ParseAlternateAccess refuses a selection of more than one element (ErrAlternateAccessUnsupported); the adapter answers DataAccessError object-access-unsupported. Single elements and components work

knownLimitations.capability: Alternate access read/write (array element, index range, component)
knownLimitations.reason: mms.Conn Read and Write take whole variables only; the client emits ok:false error unsupported for these steps

knownLimitations.capability: Write to a named variable list
knownLimitations.reason: mms.Conn Write takes a list of variables, not a variableListName; the step is unsupported and the reads that check its effect (including the InformationReport values) see the unwritten values
the client has no aa-specific ObjectName or name-list scope; define, attributes, read, write, delete and get-name-list in aa scope are unsupported
FileOpenAt drops the lastModified attribute of the response; the client reports 0
the server builds the type description from the value, so an Enum (INT8) is described as Integer(32) and iec61850bean cannot map the node; libiec61850 clients are not affected

knownLimitations.capability: Write of FC ST (and the dchg report it would trigger)
knownLimitations.reason: server.WithWritableFCs ignores ST/MX/OR/EX/SG by design (status is read-only in IEC 61850-7-2), so the write is always object-access-denied; the libiec61850 server denies it as well today
